name: Distilling and transferring what models learn
gist: Papers compress large pretrained models and transfer their knowledge to new domains through knowledge distillation and diffusion models, making powerful representations accessible on limited devices.
explain: Large models trained on billions of weights are effective but expensive to run. A smartphone or an edge device cannot run a model that requires gigabytes of memory and thousands of arithmetic operations per prediction. Knowledge distillation is the answer: train a small 'student' model to mimic a large 'teacher' model, capturing the essential patterns in a compact form. The teacher model is often self-supervised pretrained on huge unlabeled datasets, and the student inherits that knowledge without ever seeing the original data — the teacher has already distilled the patterns into its weights.

The difficulty is that small models cannot physically represent everything a large model knows. A 1-million-weight model cannot learn as much as a 1-billion-weight model. So the distillation process involves strategic choices: what information from the teacher is most important to preserve? How should the student's output distribution be compared to the teacher's? Should you distill layer by layer or just final outputs? Diffusion models add another dimension: some papers use diffusion-based distillation, where the student learns to denoise in a different way than the teacher, or where distillation itself becomes a denoising process. The quality loss is unavoidable, but well-done distillation can recover 80-95% of the teacher's performance in a model 10x smaller.

Across 17 papers, researchers develop distillation techniques for self-supervised models, study what knowledge transfers and what does not, and explore whether distillation across domains or architectures is possible. Papers also study domain transfer: can a model trained on general internet images learn representations that transfer to a specific domain like medical imaging or satellite photos? The practical value is clear: it enables on-device AI by reducing memory footprint, reduces computational costs because prediction becomes faster, and makes good representations accessible to resource-constrained applications like mobile phones or IoT sensors that could never run a model with billions of weights.

papers.title: CrossQ: Task-Aligned Cross-Token Conditional Quantization for Late Interaction Retrieval
papers.contribution: Achieves 64x raw token-storage reduction while maintaining 98% of full-precision ColBERT performance at 8 B/token.

papers.title: MaRS: Memory-Adaptive Routing for Reliable Capacity Expansion and Knowledge Retention
papers.contribution: Achieves state-of-the-art continual learning performance with frozen LPMs through controlled slot expansion and dual-stage contrastive-distillation adaptation that preserves prior knowledge without raw replay.

papers.title: Plug-and-Play Compositionality for Boosting Continual Learning with Foundation Models
papers.contribution: CompSLOT significantly enhances various continual learners and provides a universal concept-level module for reducing catastrophic forgetting.

papers.title: Reconstruct Anything Model a lightweight foundation model for computational imaging
papers.contribution: Achieves state-of-the-art performance across medical imaging to low-photon imaging and microscopy, with few-shot fine-tuning capability without ground-truth references.

papers.title: Towards Improved Sentence Representations using Token Graphs
papers.contribution: Maintains 97% accuracy when 90% of tokens are distractors, competitive with SOTA on GLUE/MTEB with 20x fewer parameters and 100x faster than parameter-efficient finetuning.

papers.title: Active Learning with Foundation Model Priors: Efficient Learning under Class Imbalance
papers.contribution: Achieve over 50% annotation savings compared to best baselines while preserving performance and robustness to label noise across imbalanced image and text datasets.

papers.title: Cutting the Skip: Training Residual-Free Transformers
papers.contribution: Demonstrates the first method enabling stable training of skipless vision transformers that outperform residual baselines on dense prediction tasks while learning richer hierarchical representations.

papers.title: Differentiable JPEG-based Input Perturbation for Knowledge Distillation Amplification via Conditional Mutual Information Maximization
papers.contribution: Improves student accuracy by up to 4.11% while remaining computationally lightweight and compatible with standard KD pipelines.

papers.title: Distilling Linearized Behavior into Non-linear Fine-Tuning for Effective Task Arithmetic
papers.contribution: Distilled model inherits linearization properties for task arithmetic without inference overhead, achieving effective composition across vision and language.

papers.title: DomED: Redesigning Ensemble Distillation for Domain Generalization
papers.contribution: Achieves competitive accuracies and substantially improved uncertainty estimates across multiple domain generalization benchmarks.

papers.title: GeoPurify: A Data-Efficient Geometric Distillation Framework for Open-Vocabulary 3D Segmentation
papers.contribution: GeoPurify achieves or surpasses state-of-the-art performance utilizing only ~1.5% of typical training data on major 3D benchmarks.

papers.title: IVQ: Structured and Lightweight Vector Quantization via Binary Hierarchical Composition Inspired by $\textit{IChing}$
papers.contribution: Achieves superior quality with significantly smaller codebooks and consistently higher utilization rates compared to VQ variants in audio representation, with cross-modal generation validating universality.

papers.title: InfoAtlas: A Foundation Model for Zero-Shot Statistical Dependence Estimate
papers.contribution: Matches state-of-the-art neural estimators in accuracy while achieving 100x speedup, generalizes to complex real-world scenarios.

papers.title: Learning Graph Foundation Models on Riemannian Graph-of-Graphs
papers.contribution: Theoretical analysis shows that R-GFM reduces structural domain generalization error compared to fixed-scale GFMs

papers.title: Multimodal Dataset Distillation via Phased Teacher Models
papers.contribution: PTM-ST achieves up to 13.5% absolute improvement and an average gain of 9.53% on Flickr30k while reducing storage overhead.

papers.title: SPEAR: A Unified SSL Framework for Learning Speech and Audio Representations
papers.contribution: Establishes new state-of-the-art on SUPERB benchmark, surpassing WavLM Large on 12 of 15 tasks while achieving competitive HEAR performance.

papers.title: SiNGER: A Clearer Voice Distills Vision Transformers Further
papers.contribution: Consistently improves student models achieving state-of-the-art on downstream tasks with clearer, more interpretable representations.
